correctness.rationale: The factorial-moment equivalence is correct: exchangeable conditioning on K converts the first three factorial moments exactly into three-wise-independent fair bits. After writing K=r+qJ, the prescribed moments become a mean, variance n/(4q^2), and zero centered third moment. The cubic-polynomial lattice inequalities in the package give the exact low-variance obstruction for a given fractional mean; the explicit high-variance zero-skew four-point law brackets the target at n=q^2+2 and convex interpolation uses at most five J-values. Below q^2-1, nearest-integer variance already blocks one residue; at q^2-1,q^2,q^2+1 the displayed residues violate the sharper zero-third-moment minimum. The fetched exact-rational verifier independently checks constructions through q=200 and the boundary formulas, but the proof is analytic.
